chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from his brother Al-Hasan, from Zur'ah, from Sama'ah, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about a slave girl of a group who went to a tribe other than her own tribe and informed them that she was a free woman. So a man from them married her, and she gave birth to him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'His children are slaves, except if the proof is established that a witness testified for her that she was a free woman, so her children would not be owned and they would be free.'
ai.seo_question: What is the status of children born to a slave woman who marries a free man?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the status of offspring in cases of marital deception regarding a woman's freedom, establishing that children remain slaves unless a witness testifies to her free status at the time of marriage. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle of 'presumption of continuity' (istishab), where the default state of slavery persists unless proven otherwise, ensuring legal certainty in family lineage. It serves as a foundational text for understanding how conditional claims of freedom impact the social and legal standing of descendants in classical fiqh.
